model_annotation: The plot illustrates the development of exports, imports, and the trade balance (saldo) over time, measured in billions of US dollars (Mrd. US-Dollar). The x-axis represents time, spanning from early 2020 to late 2023, with labeled years at regular intervals and monthly tick marks, using a linear scale. The y-axis on the left, corresponding to exports and imports, ranges from 0 to 400 in increments of 50, also on a linear scale. The y-axis on the right, corresponding to the trade balance (saldo), ranges from -200 to 400 in increments of 100, also linear. The blue line (imports) starts at approximately 200 billion USD in early 2020, dips to around 160 billion USD in mid-2020, then rises steadily to about 280 billion USD by mid-2022, fluctuates slightly, and then increases sharply to approximately 350 billion USD by late 2023. The purple line (exports) begins at about 130 billion USD in early 2020, drops to roughly 90 billion USD in mid-2020, then gradually increases to around 170 billion USD by mid-2022, and remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations, ending near 180 billion USD in late 2023. The blue bars (saldo) represent the trade balance, using the right y-axis scale. They start near 70 billion USD in early 2020, dip below zero to about -40 billion USD in mid-2020, then rise to approximately 80 billion USD by mid-2021, remain mostly positive with small fluctuations until late 2022, and then turn negative, reaching about -150 billion USD by late 2023.
